nonNegotiableRules: There is no 'available performance %': the only figures are the cooling potential from the host's power-headroom method (level A) and the measured guided result — StatusHero.performance is optional for this reason; never fabricate a value for it.

No user-facing copy lives in this package — this includes accessible-only text (aria-label, title, alt, placeholder), not just visible text; every string is a prop supplied by the app's ES/EN catalog. examples/*.example.svelte are the one exception, hardcoding Spanish for demo brevity.
CausalRail has no empty state — do not render it with insufficient evidence, and do not mount it below a 980px shell width.
BottomBar: the 'Ahora' item is always index 0.
accent-blue is never a status/alert color.
Elevation is a 1px hairline border only — never add box-shadow or a shadow token.
Do not add a web font — the sans stack already resolves to Segoe UI on Windows.
Button's 'destructive' variant is only for a Dialog's confirm button, never the row/entry-point control that opens that dialog.

Do not draw new onboarding illustrations in a different visual style (e.g. Corporate Memphis / human figures) without the user explicitly asking for that departure — the 5 shipped illustrations, the app icon and NavIcon share one abstract, geometric vocabulary on purpose.

OnboardingFlow has no business logic and never will — slide 5's detection state (status/coverage/advancedAccessAvailable) is driven entirely by the steps[4] prop object, never computed or simulated inside the component.

SettingsScreen has no business logic and never will — every disabled state, dependency reason, sensor-coverage status, and update-flow status is a prop the host computes; its only local state is whether its two destructive-action confirmation dialogs are open.

SessionsScreen/GuidedDiagnosticScreen/CpuScreen/AnalysisScreen/ReportScreen have no business logic either — status/phase/groups/rows/tracks/events and every narrative string are host-computed props; the only local state any of them owns is view-only UI state (dialog-open, metric-mode toggle, table filter/sort/scroll).

CpuAdvancedTable's virtualization and AnalysisChart's chart are hand-rolled, not a dependency — this system ships zero runtime dependencies; extend the existing hand-rolled approach rather than adding a virtualization or charting library.
A null sample in AnalysisTrack.points is a real gap, never bridged by interpolation — AnalysisChart breaks the line into separate segments around it.

ReportScreen never fabricates impactValue — same rule as StatusHero.performance applied to the Informe screen; omit impactValue and supply impactUnavailableTitle/impactUnavailableReason instead when no method applies (power limit unknown, no guided result).
A ReportScreen section with empty/undefined content is omitted entirely, never rendered as a padded stub.

An ARIA role must match real behavior — never assign role/aria-valuenow/aria-valuetext etc. without the interaction to back them up. AnalysisChart's .brush is role="slider" only because arrow keys really move aria-valuenow (see its keyboard model); its outer <svg class="plot"> is role="group", not role="img", because it contains real focusable role="button" event bands.
AnalysisChart is the definitive production chart, not a placeholder for ECharts — see AGENTS.md "AnalysisChart: SVG vs. ECharts" for the verified performance envelope and point-budget guidance.

AnalysisChart.notes: Hand-rolled SVG, zero dependencies — the definitive production implementation, not a placeholder for ECharts (see AGENTS.md "AnalysisChart: SVG vs. ECharts" for the verified performance envelope: first render stayed under 300ms and keyboard-cursor latency stayed single-digit-ms up to 20,000 points/track x 4 tracks + 100 event bands). One <svg> stacks all tracks by Y-offset so one pointer-move handler draws one shared cursor. A null point value is a real gap, never interpolated — each track draws as one <path> per contiguous gap-free/quality-consistent run, not one node per point. Legend-swatch show/hide is local view-only state. The .brush strip below the plot is a real role="slider" (arrow keys move aria-valuenow, Home/End jump to extremes, Enter/Space arms then commits a range, Escape cancels an armed-not-committed selection) with a visible rangeSummaryLabel sentence and a visually-hidden real <table> as the textual/tabular alternative. The outer <svg class="plot"> is role="group", not role="img", since it has real focusable role="button" event-band children.
